newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESTONIA-ANALYSTS SAY EESTI GAAS, OLUMPIA PRICES HIGH.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIA-ANALYSTS SAY EESTI GAAS, OLUMPIA PRICES HIGH.

text.p: The average prices of Eesti Gaas and Hotel Olumpia shares in their public offering were higher than expected, analysts said on Wednesday.
Analysts differed on what price Eesti Gaas and Hotel Olumpia shares would reach on the OTC market after their minority shares were sold publicly.
The average price of Olumpia's shares was 525 voucher kroons while the average price for Eesti Gaas was 8,506 voucher kroons.
Voucher kroons were distributed to the population as part of the privatisation process to compensate for Soviet seizures of property.
Privatisation vouchers closed at 0.338 kroons on Wednesday on the Tallinn bourse but the price had risen to 0.48 kroons during the week before the subscription period closed.
One analyst said Olumpia will not rise on the OTC market very much as investors had anticipated its future increase by making high offers.
But another analyst said Olumpia's solid half-year results gave it plenty of room to rise.
Analysts said the average price of Eesti Gaas was high compared to its present OTC market price of around 2,100 kroons.
"There will be no activity at such a high price," an analyst said.
Another analyst said its present shareholders Ruhrgas and Gazprom might raise their stake and the increased demand may take the price up.
But upward movement in the firm's price will be held in check by its 1997 profit forecast that it will just break even, analysts said.
